text:
Closest evidence: [Petrov & Macdonald, RecSys 2022](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643v2) study Recency-based Sampling of Sequences (RSS), sampling targets with probability proportional to α^(n−k). On MovieLens-20M, intermediate recency weighting outperformed both terminal-only continuation and uniform target sampling; effective ranges included α=0.2–0.9 for Caser/SASRec and 0.6–0.9 for GRU4Rec. However, RSS removes multiple sampled targets and predicts them jointly from remaining interactions; it is not a controlled comparison of uniformly sampled versus recent-biased prefix cutoffs. BERT4Rec was a comparison baseline, not an RSS-trained architecture. Thus, these findings support investigating recency weighting but do not establish its independent benefit under fixed terminal-mask supervision.

Elapsed time and interaction position should be distinguished. [Uniform Sequence Better, AAAI 2023](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25540) reports that histories with more uniform inter-event intervals improve recommendation relative to histories with highly variable intervals, and introduces time-aware augmentation controlled by sequence length. This supports examining temporal irregularity and length as moderators, but does not demonstrate an interaction with recent-cutoff oversampling.

The specific causal question remains unresolved by these sources. A useful BERT4Rec ablation would hold appended-mask supervision, auxiliary masking, optimizer, training steps and terminal-cutoff probability constant while varying only the distribution over nonterminal cutoffs: uniform versus recent-biased. Report fixed-protocol validation HR@10 by history length and timestamp-gap strata. This would separate cutoff recency from extra terminal supervision and reveal whether any benefit depends on interaction count or elapsed time.
